subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: generates the weak laser pulses or single photons that encode the key bits.

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: carries single photons between the two parties without amplification.

subsystems.name: Single-photon detectors
subsystems.role: detect individual photons at very low light levels.

subsystems.name: Classical post-processing
subsystems.role: turns raw detection events into a shared secret key.

subsystems.name: Key management layer
subsystems.role: stores keys and supplies them to encryptors on demand.

subsystems.name: Trusted nodes (for long links)
subsystems.role: relay keys across distances beyond a single fibre span, at the cost of trusting the node.

buildSteps.title: Select protocol and link type
buildSteps.detail: Choose a protocol such as BB84 (polarisation or phase encoding) and decide between fibre or free-space satellite transmission.

buildSteps.title: Install the quantum channel
buildSteps.detail: Lay dedicated dark fibre between sites or set up a ground station with a telescope for satellite passes.

buildSteps.title: Build transmitter and receiver
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the laser, modulators, detectors and timing electronics at each end of the link.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the optics
buildSteps.detail: Align polarisation, adjust detector gates and verify that photon counts match expectations.

buildSteps.title: Run quantum transmission
buildSteps.detail: Send photons one by one; the receiver records detection times and measurement bases.

buildSteps.title: Sift and correct errors
buildSteps.detail: Over an authenticated classical channel, compare bases to keep matching events, then correct bit errors.

buildSteps.title: Amplify privacy
buildSteps.detail: Hash the key down to remove any information an eavesdropper might have gained, leaving a secret key.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryptors
buildSteps.detail: Feed the keys into AES or one-time-pad systems that protect the actual data traffic.

buildSteps.title: Operate and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Continuously generate keys and watch for disturbances that signal interception or fibre faults.

prerequisites.why: needed to register individual photons without adding noise that would hide an eavesdropper.
photon loss limits range; standard telecom fibre is used, but loss grows with distance.
post-processing messages must be authenticated to stop a man-in-the-middle attack.
without them, fibre links are limited to roughly 100–200 km before trusted nodes are required.
demonstrated by the Micius satellite, but only for limited passes and not yet a commercial service.

pathway.milestone: metro QKD links and satellite demonstrations (e.g. Micius)
pathway.unlocks: eavesdropper-evident key exchange over tens to hundreds of kilometres.

pathway.milestone: intercity QKD networks built from trusted nodes
pathway.unlocks: secure key distribution between cities, as in early national testbeds.

pathway.milestone: standards and integration with telecom equipment
pathway.unlocks: easier deployment alongside existing fibre and encryption gear.
long-distance quantum networks and a future quantum internet, removing the need to trust intermediate nodes.
